human-interface-guidelines: Start with the target platform, then connect the relevant foundation, task pattern, component, input, and integration guidance.
getting-started: Use the platform introductions to establish interaction expectations before choosing components or visual styling.
design-principles: Evaluate whether the experience serves a meaningful purpose, supports familiar behavior, and accommodates different contexts.
Treat wording, feedback, transitions, and ongoing refinement as part of product quality.
designing-for-ios: Prioritize the primary mobile task and check reachability, touch interaction, system navigation, and interruption recovery.
Adapt to supported displays and accessibility settings instead of treating one phone screenshot as the layout contract.
designing-for-ipados: Design for changing window sizes and combinations of touch, keyboard, pointer, and Apple Pencil.
Use available space to support the task and its context; verify multitasking rather than merely enlarging phone layouts.
designing-for-macos: Support sustained work through window management, menus, keyboard navigation, and appropriate document or selection behavior.
Choose familiar Mac controls and preserve context across resizing, multiple windows, and switching applications.
designing-for-tvos: Check readability from a television viewing distance and navigation through remote focus.
Keep content easy to reach with a predictable focus path and visible selection feedback.
designing-for-visionos: Choose windows, volumes, and immersion according to the task and the person's physical surroundings.
Evaluate targeting, viewing comfort, passthrough, and transitions with spatial input rather than assuming a flat-screen layout transfers unchanged.
designing-for-watchos: Make useful information available in short interactions with clear, easily operated controls.
Consider the Digital Crown, complications, notifications, and glanceable content as connected entry points into the task.
designing-for-games: Get people into play promptly with useful defaults and instruction integrated into gameplay.
Request setup or permissions when their purpose becomes clear, and support the platform's input and accessibility expectations.
designing-for-iphone-duo: Preserve the current task when the device changes display configuration.
Consult the current device article for display and transition guidance; avoid fixed-size assumptions that discard context.
foundations: Review accessibility, layout, typography, color, materials, privacy, and writing together because they shape every screen.
accessibility: Check whether people can perceive the content, understand the controls, and complete the task with their preferred access methods.
Verify larger text and meaningful alternatives to visual, auditory, gesture-only, or motion-dependent information.
app-icons: Create a recognizable identity with clear shapes and layers that remain legible in the system's presentations.
Use the current platform templates and production tools; check appearance variants before exporting assets.
branding: Express identity through purposeful content, language, accent color, and typography while retaining recognizable interaction conventions.
Apply distinctive styling where it strengthens the task rather than making standard controls harder to identify.
color: Assign consistent semantic meaning to colors and provide another cue for important distinctions.
Evaluate the palette in both appearances, higher contrast, different lighting, and supported displays.
dark-mode: Respect system appearance and evaluate images, text, and surfaces in both light and dark contexts.
Use adaptive semantic values so custom backgrounds do not undermine contrast or hierarchy.
icons: Use simple recognizable forms with consistent visual weight and optical alignment.
Choose familiar action metaphors and supply meaningful accessible descriptions where the icon carries information.
images: Provide appropriate resolution and color information for supported displays.
Test real-device presentation and cropping instead of assuming a source asset's dimensions guarantee visual quality.
immersive-experiences: Choose immersion deliberately and keep the person's awareness and comfort central to transitions.
Use environmental dimming or unbounded content only when it supports attention and the intended spatial experience.
inclusion: Review copy and representations from perspectives beyond the design team's own experience.
Prefer understandable language and avoid assumptions about identity, ability, culture, or how people use the product.
layout: Express importance through grouping, alignment, and predictable placement before adding decoration.
Verify resizing, safe areas, text expansion, changing device configurations, and progressive disclosure.
materials: Use material to communicate interface layering and hierarchy, with clear separation between content and controls.
Consult current Liquid Glass guidance for placement and variants; evaluate contrast and avoid applying the effect indiscriminately.
motion: Use animation to explain feedback, relationships, and transitions while keeping the task responsive.
Respect reduced-motion preferences and offer an understandable experience without decorative movement.
privacy: Ask for the data needed for the current feature and explain the purpose where the request is made.
Prefer system privacy protections and on-device processing when appropriate; make data use understandable.
right-to-left: Check alignment and directional behavior using the language of the content and platform conventions.
Test numbers, mixed-language text, symbols, and navigation individually rather than reversing every element.
sf-symbols: Choose symbols that communicate the intended concept and align with surrounding text and control weight.
Check rendering mode, localization, accessibility, and availability rather than using a symbol name as a complete asset specification.
spatial-layout: Place important content within a comfortable viewing area and account for depth and surrounding space.
Avoid layouts that force sustained awkward viewing or attach interface content rigidly to head movement.
typography: Use readable text styles and a clear hierarchy across supported display and viewing contexts.
Verify weight, contrast, text scaling, and localization together instead of specifying font size alone.
writing: Use a consistent product voice and adjust tone to the person's situation.
Make labels and instructions precise, concise, inclusive, and directly connected to the action or outcome.
patterns: Select guidance by the person's task and include entry, pending work, completion, interruption, and recovery.
charting-data: Choose a chart when it clarifies a meaningful relationship or comparison in the data.
Keep the initial presentation understandable and provide accessible ways to explore detail.
collaboration-and-sharing: Make sharing easy to find and describe collaboration permissions in understandable terms.
Use the platform sharing experience and make the difference between sending a copy and shared editing clear.
drag-and-drop: Support predictable movement or copying of appropriate content and communicate the result at the destination.
Provide another way to perform the operation and consider multiple-item transfers.
entering-data: Reduce unnecessary entry with available system information and clearly explain required fields.
Choose suitable secure entry and validation behavior without inventing or prepopulating sensitive credentials.
feedback: Place routine status near the affected interaction and reserve interruption for decisions needing attention.
Make feedback perceivable through appropriate alternatives and explain unexpected irreversible loss before commitment.
file-management: Integrate familiar document creation, opening, and keyboard commands with the platform file model.
Preserve work predictably and make explicit deletion or cancellation distinguishable from ordinary navigation.
going-full-screen: Use full screen when it benefits the activity while preserving access to essential controls.
Adapt layout without surprising window changes and retain expected system escape and navigation behavior.
launching: Show useful content promptly and restore context so people can resume their work.
Treat required launch presentation separately from onboarding and avoid making a branding screen a routine delay.
live-viewing-apps: Make live content prominent and quick to start while clearly communicating that it is live.
Provide useful progress or event context without obscuring the viewing experience.
loading: Present useful information early and allow unrelated activity while work continues.
Explain unavoidable delays and consider background delivery of large assets where the platform supports it.
managing-accounts: Explain account benefits and defer authentication until the task requires it.
Use recognizable authentication methods and consult platform guidance for passkeys and Sign in with Apple.
managing-notifications: Match interruption level to actual urgency and relevance rather than engagement goals.
Keep promotional messaging subject to permission and separate from genuinely time-sensitive events.
modality: Use interruption for a bounded task with a clear benefit and a reliable return path.
Keep modal work focused; reassess a flow that grows into an entire secondary application.
multitasking: Preserve state as people switch tasks, resize windows, or encounter audio interruptions.
Finish appropriate initiated work in the background while pausing activities that need active participation.
offering-help: Offer guidance for actual task difficulties using the same terms and visuals as the interface.
Keep assistance contextual and useful instead of documenting every familiar system control.
onboarding: Teach unfamiliar behavior through relevant interaction and timely contextual guidance.
Keep prerequisites brief and make extended instruction optional when the task permits it.
playing-audio: Respect the person's audio environment, interruptions, output routes, and system volume control.
Choose audio behavior according to the task and verify coexistence with other sound.
playing-haptics: Use established haptic meanings consistently and sparingly.
Complement other feedback so understanding the result does not depend on feeling a vibration.
playing-video: Prefer familiar playback controls and preserve the video's aspect ratio.
Evaluate presentation, captions, transport controls, and interruptions for the supported platforms.
printing: Make printing discoverable when it is supported and present only relevant options.
Use platform printing UI before introducing application-specific print settings.
ratings-and-reviews: Ask after meaningful engagement at a moment that does not interrupt the person's task.
Use the system rating mechanism and avoid repeated requests that become pressure.
searching: Give search a discoverable place that matches its importance to the task.
Communicate scope and provide useful suggestions and understandable results.
settings: Start with strong defaults and expose settings only when people have a meaningful reason to change them.
Place preferences where the platform expects them and avoid using settings as a substitute for thoughtful setup.
undo-and-redo: Make reversals predictable and show their effects in the affected content.
Support a useful sequence of undoable work and label history actions by what they change.
workouts: Prioritize relevant live data and easily operated workout controls.
Make the active session apparent and avoid unrelated interruptions during physical activity.
components: Choose a component for its interaction semantics and platform behavior, then verify its article's platform considerations.
content: Select content views according to the information being presented, edited, compared, or played.
layout-and-organization: Use containers to express real hierarchy and relationships while preserving navigation and selection during resizing.
menus-and-actions: Distinguish commands from navigation and value selection, and make important actions discoverable.
navigation-and-search: Make location, hierarchy, current selection, and search scope understandable throughout a task.
presentation: Choose the least disruptive presentation that provides sufficient space and a clear completion or dismissal path.
selection-and-input: Choose controls by value type, number of choices, precision, and supported input methods.
status: Communicate current state and progress where the information is useful without demanding unnecessary attention.
system-experiences: Adapt content and actions to the constraints of system surfaces rather than reproducing a full app screen.
activity-rings: Use Activity rings for their established activity measurements and a single person's progress.
Preserve their system meaning and appearance instead of repurposing them as generic metrics.
activity-views: Offer context-appropriate sharing and actions through the familiar system activity presentation.
Avoid duplicating existing activities and give custom actions concise identifiable labels.
alerts: Interrupt for a consequential decision or actionable problem rather than routine information.
Prefer less disruptive feedback for reversible everyday actions and avoid an alert as the first launch experience.
action-sheets: Offer a concise set of choices connected to an action the person intentionally started.
Keep explanatory text short and use the platform's appropriate action-sheet or alternative presentation.
boxes: Group a manageable set of related controls with spacing and alignment that clarify their relationship.
Add a short descriptive heading only when it improves understanding.
buttons: Make the action clear through its label, visual emphasis, semantic role, and interaction feedback.
Check platform target sizes and custom pressed states; reserve destructive semantics for actions that can remove data.
charts: Choose marks and axis ranges to preserve the meaning of the intended comparison.
Check labels, scales, accessibility, and whether combined marks clarify rather than distort the data.
collections: Use recognizable grid or row arrangements for browsable items and make selection straightforward.
Consider a table for primarily textual records and add custom interactions only when the task benefits.
color-wells: Represent color selection with a recognizable well and prefer the system color picker for adjustment.
column-views: Expose successive hierarchy levels in adjacent columns, beginning with the root.
Allow useful column sizing and consider a preview or details for a selected leaf item.
combo-boxes: Use a combo box when the person can select a suggestion or enter a value.
Provide relevant options, a meaningful initial value where appropriate, and a label explaining the expected content.
complications: Surface essential changing information that is useful at a glance.
Support relevant complication families and route activation to the associated detail or task.
context-menus: Keep commands few and relevant to the selected object or context.
Expose essential functionality through other discoverable interface paths as well.
controls: Offer quick system-surface actions that are useful without opening the full app.
Use a meaningful symbol and keep the displayed state consistent with completed or remotely changed actions.
digit-entry-views: Explain why a short digit sequence is requested and use secure entry where its meaning requires privacy.
disclosure-controls: Hide secondary details behind a recognizable disclosure control when they are not immediately needed.
Use a descriptive label and make the expanded or collapsed state understandable.
dock-menus: Provide a small set of valuable Mac commands through the Dock menu.
Keep those tasks available elsewhere so the menu is an additional entry point.
edit-menus: Preserve standard editing commands and the gestures that reveal them.
Show commands appropriate to the selection and place custom operations near related standard ones.
gauges: Explain the current measurement and its meaningful range with concise labels.
Use appearance to reinforce the quantity's interpretation rather than substituting a gauge for task progress.
home-screen-quick-actions: Choose a stable set of high-value tasks with clear titles and familiar symbols.
Route each shortcut directly to the promised task rather than a generic landing screen.
image-views: Use an image view to present visual content and assess contrast when adding overlaid text.
Use appropriate icon or symbol components when the content represents an interface command.
image-wells: Make the current image and replacement behavior understandable.
Support standard clipboard commands when applicable and provide sensible behavior when no custom image remains.
labels: Use labels for brief noneditable information with readable typography and semantic emphasis.
Allow useful text to be selected when doing so helps the person's task.
lists-and-tables: Present textual records in scannable rows with concise content and clear selection feedback.
Support editing and appropriate row interactions where they belong to the task.
live-activities: Represent a real ongoing event with a defined start and finish using concise current information.
Avoid advertising and unnecessary exposure of sensitive content on these glanceable surfaces.
lockups: Use consistent image-and-text grouping and spacing so related television content is easy to scan.
Keep neighboring items visually coherent and evaluate focus presentation.
menus: Use concise command labels and a predictable organization.
Represent unavailable actions according to platform expectations and check current guidance for icons and shortcuts.
notifications: Make each notification informative and useful without repeatedly announcing the same event.
Distinguish external updates from problems best explained in the active interface.
ornaments: Place frequently needed spatial controls near their window without crowding the content.
Evaluate stable placement, width, and visual balance when more than one ornament is present.
outline-views: Use expandable rows for genuinely hierarchical data and expose hierarchy consistently in the first column.
Provide meaningful headings and appropriate sorting; use a flat table when the records have no hierarchy.
page-controls: Indicate position within a manageable ordered set of pages.
Place the indicator predictably and keep any custom page symbols easy to distinguish.
panels: Keep related inspection or adjustment tools close to the content being edited.
Favor focused controls and a title that explains the panel's purpose.
path-controls: Represent a location or path in the content area with the appropriate standard or pop-up presentation.
Keep path display distinct from custom window-frame decoration.
pickers: Use ordered, predictable choices and select a presentation suited to their number and meaning.
Keep selection near the relevant task and use the precision people actually need.
pop-up-buttons: Use a compact selector for one value from a flat set of options.
Provide a useful initial selection and enough context to predict what the control contains.
popovers: Present a limited amount of contextual information or functionality near its source.
Verify anchoring, available space, and dismissal behavior on each target platform.
progress-indicators: Show measurable progress when it is known and an appropriate ongoing-work indication otherwise.
Keep reporting accurate and transition to determinate progress when the operation provides enough information.
pull-down-buttons: Group related commands behind a clearly labeled action control.
Keep frequently needed actions easy to reach instead of placing every operation in one menu.
rating-indicators: Make a displayed rating understandable and make adjustment easy when editing is supported.
Use a recognizable symbol and keep read-only and editable behavior clear.
scroll-views: Preserve familiar scrolling inputs and communicate that more content is available.
Avoid competing same-direction scroll regions unless the interaction has been carefully justified and tested.
search-fields: Explain searchable content or scope and offer timely results or suggestions.
Keep results easy to interpret and avoid making people infer the field's purpose from placement alone.
segmented-controls: Expose a small coherent group of related choices with visible selection state.
Use consistent content types and avoid crowding too many segments into the available space.
sheets: Use a sheet for a focused temporary task with clear completion and cancellation.
Reconsider the presentation when the flow becomes prolonged or its navigation obscures the underlying task.
sidebars: Organize destinations or content hierarchies with understandable grouping and selection.
Support disclosure and customization when useful while preserving readable content as the layout adapts.
sliders: Use a slider for a range where relative adjustment matters, with familiar directional behavior.
Provide another precise entry method when needed and use the dedicated system approach for audio volume.
snippets: Keep assistant-presented results legible and focused within their constrained presentation.
Coordinate dialogue, custom result content, and system-provided actions so the next step is clear.
split-views: Preserve the relationship between selected content and its detail across panes.
Design transitions through compact and intermediate widths and support meaningful transfers between panes.
status-bars: Account for the system status region in content presentation.
Hide it temporarily only when appropriate to the experience and preserve expected access to system information.
steppers: Keep the affected numeric value visibly associated with increment and decrement controls.
Offer a faster or direct entry method when the range makes repeated steps inefficient.
tab-bars: Use tabs for primary destinations with understandable identities and stable access.
Choose a manageable set of destinations and consult platform guidance for adaptation and overflow.
tab-views: Group closely related content areas under descriptive tabs.
Keep a pane's controls scoped to its own content and avoid replacing tab selection with an unrelated control metaphor.
text-fields: Request short values with clear context, appropriate sizing, and the right entry behavior.
Use secure entry for private values and make the purpose understandable beyond transient placeholder text.
text-views: Use a text view for substantial, editable, or specially formatted text.
Preserve legibility, appropriate keyboard behavior, and useful selection or editing interactions.
the-menu-bar: Integrate application commands with established Mac menu structure and keyboard equivalents.
Keep the command organization stable so availability changes do not make menu locations unpredictable.
toggles: Represent a clearly named binary state with a visibly distinguishable current value.
Choose the platform-appropriate toggle style and verify that its placement makes the affected setting clear.
token-fields: Use tokens to make structured selections understandable within text entry.
Provide helpful suggestions and editing or conversion commands appropriate to the represented values.
toolbars: Prioritize commands relevant to the current view and leave sufficient space for understandable controls.
Place secondary actions in an appropriate additional menu and check adaptation at narrower sizes.
top-shelf: Offer a useful television entry point into fresh or personally relevant content.
Route directly to that content and keep the surface focused on viewing rather than advertising.
virtual-keyboards: Choose an input layout appropriate to the value being entered.
Verify keyboard presentation and editing behavior without assuming a specific hardware or software keyboard is present.
watch-faces: Help people preview and share faces that meaningfully showcase available complications.
Consider device compatibility and explain unsupported choices gracefully.
web-views: Provide appropriate navigation for embedded web content and distinguish its role from the native task.
Use the platform's browser experience when the goal is general browsing rather than embedded content.
widgets: Choose focused information and interactions that remain useful at a glance.
Check each supported family and system context and route deeper work to the corresponding place in the app.
windows: Support fluid resizing and multiple-window workflows where appropriate to the platform.
Open windows at meaningful moments and preserve the standard system window controls and behavior.
inputs: Design a consistent task across the input methods each platform supports, including alternatives to specialized gestures.
action-button: Expose essential quick tasks with concise labels and use the system's instruction and activation experience.
Let the action complete within the person's current context when possible.
apple-pencil-and-scribble: Respond immediately and naturally to drawing or writing input.
Honor the person's choices about Pencil and finger behavior and account for supported pressure or device interactions.
camera-control: Keep capture controls recognizable with short names, suitable symbols, and meaningful value units.
Identify important slider values and verify the hardware interaction on supported devices.
digital-crown: Use Crown input for predictable navigation or data inspection according to the current context.
Provide visible feedback that follows the speed and direction of the interaction.
eyes: Design comfortable visual targets using standard components where possible.
Offer alternative interaction methods and verify spatial placement rather than relying on visual appearance alone.
focus-and-selection: Keep focus transitions under the person's control and use familiar platform focus presentation.
Distinguish the item receiving input from selected content and maintain understandable movement between controls.
game-controls: Choose controls appropriate to the game and platform, with clear visual and tactile feedback.
Check reachability and target size when virtual controls overlay gameplay.
gestures: Honor familiar gesture meanings and respond promptly.
Provide another way to complete important actions and communicate unavailable interactions.
gyro-and-accelerometer: Use motion sensing for a concrete benefit and assess whether movement is comfortable and appropriate.
Avoid making ordinary interface manipulation depend on device movement without a compelling task reason.
keyboards: Support efficient keyboard navigation and preserve established command shortcuts.
Choose additional shortcuts for frequent app-specific tasks and check Full Keyboard Access.
nearby-interactions: Relate physical distance and direction to a meaningful task with continuous understandable feedback.
Consider how movement changes the interaction instead of treating proximity as a context-free trigger.
pointing-devices: Preserve standard mouse and trackpad gestures and provide coherent behavior across other supported inputs.
Verify hover, pointer access to hidden controls, and the transition between pointer and touch interaction.
remotes: Use established remote gestures and predictable focus movement.
Make the result of each gesture apparent and justify any custom interaction.
technologies: Use system integration guidance for the experience and the corresponding developer documentation for implementation contracts.
airplay: Use recognizable media playback and routing behavior and stream the content people intend to share.
Check resolution, mirroring, and playback continuity with the system player where appropriate.
always-on: Keep useful information legible with stable placement when the display enters its reduced-activity presentation.
Protect sensitive information and reduce emphasis on content that is no longer essential.
app-clips: Deliver a complete focused task or meaningful demo with minimal setup.
Prioritize the immediate native experience rather than using the clip solely as an advertisement for installation.
app-shortcuts: Expose common high-value tasks in language and options people can understand.
Check current app-schema guidance and provide appropriate clarification when a request needs more information.
apple-in-app-purchase: Integrate purchase choices into the product experience with clear names and complete billing information.
Let people understand the value before committing and consult current purchase and subscription requirements.
apple-pay: Use approved payment controls and present Apple Pay appropriately when supported and available.
Keep the action tied to payment or supported setup and verify branding and payment-sheet requirements.
augmented-reality: Offer AR on capable hardware and make virtual content behave convincingly within the environment.
Consider placement, lighting, reflection, and the person's physical movement as part of the interaction.
carekit: Explain health-data use clearly and request access when the related care feature needs it.
Keep system privacy controls authoritative rather than creating a competing permission model.
carplay: Keep the in-car experience usable without requiring interaction with or unlocking the phone.
Let people initiate playback and use the approved interaction model for the supported app category.
game-center: Place system game access where it fits menu interaction without conflicting with game controls.
Account for overlay presentation and use the provided artwork for relevant links.
generative-ai: Give people meaningful control over generative features and set understandable expectations for their results.
Evaluate inclusion, responsibility, and usefulness in the actual task rather than adding generation without a clear purpose.
healthkit: Ask for relevant health-data access at the time it becomes useful and explain the purpose.
Provide clear privacy information and rely on system settings for data-sharing permissions.
homekit: Represent homes, rooms, and accessories consistently with the system model.
Support multiple homes and related accessory details without duplicating system home settings.
icloud: Make continuity and synchronization understandable while keeping the experience straightforward.
Keep content current when possible and consider storage use rather than asking people to manage unnecessary cloud decisions.
id-verifier: Request only the identity information needed and distinguish verification from transferring personal data.
Use the required system flow and identify the requesting organization appropriately.
imessage-apps-and-stickers: Focus the extension on one coherent conversation-related experience.
Put essential interactions in the compact presentation and use expanded space for editing when appropriate.
live-photos: Preserve the moving photo as a coherent item when editing or sharing.
Apply adjustments consistently and make download and playback availability understandable.
mac-catalyst: Adapt the task for Mac keyboard, pointer, window, and multitasking expectations.
Review menus, drag and drop, and content organization rather than assuming an unchanged iPad presentation is sufficient.
machine-learning: Ask for explicit feedback only when useful and keep participation voluntary.
Explain feedback options and their effects in direct language so people can make an informed choice.
maps: Choose map presentation and emphasis according to the location task.
Support appropriate exploration, search, and clearly identifiable selection.
nfc: Explain scanning in approachable language with concise instructions.
Support appropriate reading modes and avoid suggesting that the phone must physically touch the object.
photo-editing: Keep editing integrated with the host photo experience and provide a useful preview.
Handle cancellation and discarded edits deliberately while preserving the system's extension presentation.
researchkit: Introduce the study and determine eligibility in the appropriate sequence.
Make participation and consent understandable before asking people to commit.
shareplay: Use shared activity for a meaningful real-time experience with an easy start.
Design around what participants do together and accommodate supported platforms.
shazamkit: Limit recording to what recognition needs and stop promptly.
Let people choose whether recognized music is added to their cloud library.
sign-in-with-apple: Ask for authentication at a point where account value is clear.
Use the system sign-in presentation and consider linking an existing account without creating unnecessary friction.
siri: Expose useful common tasks using the vocabulary people associate with the app.
Offer relevant results and actions rather than using assistant interactions for promotion.
tap-to-pay-on-iphone: Complete merchant setup and required administrative acceptance before a customer payment interaction.
Provide practical instruction for supported payment types and device readiness.
voiceover: Describe meaningful controls and images with useful labels and values.
Make data visualizations understandable through accessible structure and omit decorative images from spoken navigation.
wallet: Offer an understandable way to add relevant passes and group related passes when appropriate.
Use the prescribed Wallet controls and avoid presenting an add action for a pass already present.
